answer: Orchard Graph Witnessing: each agent signs the set of peers it transacts with, forming a graph; new identities must be introduced by neighbors whose own edges are corroborated across independent paths. Enforcement rule: an identity earns routing weight only when its neighborhood overlaps existing clusters at a threshold, so isolated cliques stay unweighted. A lantern signal propagates only along edges witnessed from both sides, and each node's view is checked through a prism of disjoint paths, so forged neighborhoods split apart under comparison.
